blocks.text: The immune system is not in one place: it is made of many individual cells that rush to the site of infection. These are white blood cells, which arise in the bone marrow and circulate in blood and lymph, and are also found in the lymph nodes, spleen, liver, thymus and bone marrow. There are three main kinds: monocytes, T cells and B cells; T and B cells together are called lymphocytes.

blocks.caption: Main organs of the immune system (original diagram after Figure 21.11).
blocks.long_description: The immune system is not one organ but many white blood cells that arise in the bone marrow and circulate in blood and lymph; they also gather in the lymph nodes, spleen, liver, thymus and bone marrow. T cells mature in the thymus, a small grey gland just above the heart, while B cells complete their maturation in the bone marrow.

blocks.text: Monocytes circulate in the blood and enter the interstitial fluid, where they mature into macrophages that engulf and destroy microbes and make proteins that activate helper T cells. Monocytes also mature into other phagocytes that stay in the liver, spleen, lymph nodes and other tissues, and help clear cell debris and repair tissue damage. The book says they are produced in lymphoid tissues; like other white cells they arise from stem cells in the bone marrow.

T cells develop from stem cells in the bone marrow and migrate to the thymus, a small grey gland just above the heart, where they mature and learn to identify foreign molecules (antigens) on invading microbes. Tens of millions of different T cells are made, each specialised to recognise one particular antigen, so no invader escapes being recognised by at least a few.

rows: supervise the development of T cells in the thymus

blocks.text: B cells also develop in the bone marrow but do not go to the thymus; they complete their maturation in the bone marrow and are then released into the blood and lymph. Each B cell, like a T cell, recognises a particular antigen. When it meets its antigen it divides into many plasma cells, each producing an antibody that sticks to the antigen and marks it for destruction.

blocks.prompt: Where do T cells and B cells each mature?
blocks.explanation: T cells in the thymus; B cells in the bone marrow. Both arise from stem cells in the bone marrow.

items: White cells arise in bone marrow; found in lymph nodes, spleen, liver, thymus.
Monocytes become macrophages; T cells (helper, cytotoxic, inducer, suppressor) mature in the thymus.
B cells mature in bone marrow; plasma cells make antibodies.
